entries.title: Registry Performance: Query Optimization
entries.problem: Registry queries timeout on cold-start (5s insufficient for HKLM)

applicable_lessons.lesson_summary: Caching solves cold-start, but TTL-based approach has cache invalidation complexity
applicable_lessons.decision_change: IC-021 predicted 75%, but IC-027 already solved this: implement registry caching with 5min TTL. IC-027 shows actual result: 92%, variance -8%
applicable_lessons.effort_reduction: From estimated MEDIUM to proven MEDIUM (no surprise complexity)
applicable_lessons.implementation_action: Apply IC-027 caching solution: registry query result cache with TTL invalidation

applicable_lessons.lesson_title: Timeout is a Symptom, Not Root Cause
applicable_lessons.lesson_summary: Increasing timeout from 5s→10s revealed bottleneck but didn't solve performance
applicable_lessons.decision_change: Don't increase timeout. Apply caching (IC-027) instead. IC-026 teaches: timeout extension masks real problem
applicable_lessons.expected_outcome: Solve root cause (cold-start hive load) not symptom (timeout)
applicable_lessons.implementation_action: Implement caching first, then monitor timeout behavior

implementation_plan.step_2: Cache HKLM query results with 5min TTL
implementation_plan.step_3: Monitor timeout behavior (may be eliminated by caching)
implementation_plan.step_4: Only increase timeout if caching insufficient
implementation_plan.why_lessons_apply: IC-021 is subset of IC-027. IC-026 teaches meta-lesson: fix bottleneck before timeout tuning
